strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with clear demonstration of the categorical vs. numerical generation difficulty gap (Figure 2) and practical relevance of mixed-type features
Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation across 12 diverse datasets with 13+ metrics, extensive ablation studies, and reproducibility details including promised code release
Substantial empirical improvements: 40% detection score increase over CDTD (0.423 vs 0.301), 50% WD reduction for numerical features, consistent across most datasets
Theoretically grounded approach with Theorem 1 proving data-dependent coupling tightens transport cost bounds; sound mathematical derivations of guided conditional probability paths
Principled handling of mixed-type features via cascaded decomposition with feature-specific masking strategy (Eq. 2) that naturally accommodates missing/inflated values
Honest ablation studies (Table 2) demonstrating necessity of full approach; good presentation of limitations and failure cases
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primary contribution is combining established techniques (cascaded diffusion from Ho et al. 2022, flow matching from Lipman et al. 2023, learnable schedules from CDTD/TabDiff, optimal transport couplings from Albergo et al. 2024) rather than fundamental innovation

Incomplete evaluation of mixed-type features: paper emphasizes missing value handling but lacks comprehensive assessment of zero-inflation and censoring; only simulated MNAR data tested, no real-world missing data experiments

Highly dataset-dependent performance with some datasets showing poor absolute results (electricity: 0.008, news: 0.001 detection scores across all methods); paper lacks analysis of dataset characteristics or failure modes affecting performance

Strong architectural dependency on CDTD as low-resolution model limits modularity; Table 19 shows swapping CDTD for ARF significantly degrades detection score (0.426→0.299), raising questions about whether improvements stem from cascade strategy or CDTD specifically
Encoder selection appears arbitrary: DT outperforms GMM primarily due to more components (65.5 vs 12.5), not fundamental superiority; GMM component cap at 30 seems ad-hoc

Privacy-utility tradeoff insufficiently addressed: MIA scores drop from 0.970 to 0.959 with TabCascade; high-fidelity synthesis risks merit discussion but no comparison with privacy-preserving alternatives
Learned time schedules (Appendix A.6.2) appear mostly linear in practice, questioning necessity of learnable parameterization; no explicit ablation isolating benefits of polynomial vs fixed schedules

Computational overhead underexplored: training two models adds complexity and parameter count; Table 22 shows mixed speed results (slower than some baselines), insufficient discussion of practical tradeoffs
